answer: One marble backs an operator, and each identity drawing on it must hold one live yarrow of capacity. That capacity decays every epoch at a rate multiplied by the number of identities on the marble, and a decayed yarrow is restored only by buying a fresh one in velvet, one purchase per identity. A singleton restores one yarrow per epoch; a farm of k restores k yarrows, each decaying k times as fast, so keeping a thousand clones able to act costs a million velvet purchases an epoch. Sub-keys inherit the marble and its headcount, so a split buys no discount.
